title: Resonance
notes: **Resonance:** when a single Lewis structure cannot represent a molecule accurately, two or more contributing structures are used. The true structure is a resonance hybrid.

**Example â€” carbonate ion $CO_3^{2-}$:** three equivalent resonance structures with the double bond rotating among the three oxygens. The actual bond order is 1.33, intermediate between single and double.
**Example â€” benzene $C_6H_6$:** two Kekule structures with alternating double bonds. The hybrid has equal bond lengths intermediate between single and double.
**Rules:** contributing structures must have the same atomic positions, same number of paired and unpaired electrons, and the same overall charge. They differ only in electron distribution.

**Resonance energy:** the stabilization due to resonance is the difference in energy between the hybrid and the most stable contributing structure. More resonance structures usually mean greater stability.
